questions.q: Which one of the following is the main reason many cement factories are located near limestone deposits in Nigeria?
options: To reduce raw material transport costs because limestone is bulky
Because limestone provides the energy needed for cement kilns
To obtain cheap labour from miners who work the limestone
To avoid government taxes by being in remote areas
questions.explanation: Cement production requires large quantities of bulky limestone, so locating factories near deposits minimizes transport costs. Cheap labour or tax avoidance are not the primary factors, and limestone is a raw material, not an energy source for kilns (fuel provides energy).

questions.q: A Nigerian textile firm considers two sites: Site A is close to a major cotton-producing area but far from the port; Site B is near a port but farther from cotton fields. Which factor best explains choosing Site A?
options: Lower land prices at Site A than at Site B
Greater access to export markets at the port
Minimising the cost of transporting bulky raw fibre to the factory
Availability of skilled managers in the cotton-producing area
questions.explanation: Textile factories benefit from proximity to bulky raw cotton to reduce transport costs and preserve fibre quality. While port access aids exports, the immediate priority for raw material industries is reducing input transport costs. Land price and managers are less decisive here.

questions.q: Which of the following best describes a non-renewable natural resource?
options: A resource that is recycled continuously, like water in the hydrologic cycle
A resource that is never depleted despite use, like sunlight
A resource that can be grown each year, like cassava
A resource that forms very slowly and cannot be replaced within a human lifetime, like crude oil
questions.explanation: Non-renewable resources (e.g., crude oil) form over geological time and are not replaced within human timescales. Cassava is a renewable agricultural product, sunlight is effectively inexhaustible on human timescales, and water is recycled through the hydrologic cycle.

questions.q: Which soil horizon is typically richest in humus and most important for plant growth?
options: Topsoil (A horizon)
C horizon (parent material)
R horizon (bedrock)
B horizon (subsoil)
questions.explanation: The A horizon or topsoil contains most organic matter (humus) and nutrients vital for plant roots. The B horizon is mineral-rich but less organic; the C horizon is weathered parent material and R is unweathered bedrock.

questions.q: Which feature most characterises the Guinea savanna vegetation zone of Nigeria?
options: Mangrove trees with prop roots along tidal estuaries
Sparse thorny shrubs in an arid landscape with dunes
Dense evergreen trees forming a closed canopy with many lianas
Tall grasses with scattered deciduous trees adapted to a distinct dry season
questions.explanation: Guinea savanna has tall grasses and scattered deciduous trees adapted to alternating wet and dry seasons. Dense evergreen canopy describes rainforest; sparse thorny shrubs describe Sahel/arid zones; mangroves occur in coastal tidal estuaries.

questions.q: A farmer notices hard, compacted soil with low infiltration after repeated tilling and grazing. Which soil problem is this?
options: Podzolisation from heavy leaching in humid forests
Soil compaction leading to reduced porosity
Soil salinisation caused by irrigation water
Gleying caused by permanent waterlogging with grey colours
questions.explanation: Heavy tilling and grazing can compact soil, reducing pore spaces and infiltration. Salinisation arises from evaporative accumulation of salts (often irrigated soils), podzolisation is a leaching process in cool humid climates, and gleying is due to prolonged waterlogging, not compaction alone.

questions.q: A maize farmer in Kaduna applies a fertilizer mixture containing 60 kg nitrogen (N), 30 kg phosphorus (P₂O₅) and 10 kg potassium (K₂O) per hectare. If the recommended N application is 120 kg/ha, how much more N is needed per hectare?
options: 80 kg
120 kg
60 kg
40 kg
questions.explanation: Recommended N is 120 kg/ha; current application supplies 60 kg N, so additional required = 120 − 60 = 60 kg. 40 kg or 80 kg are incorrect differences; 120 kg would double the recommended amount rather than the deficit.

questions.q: Which farming practice will best reduce soil erosion on the steep slopes of the Jos Plateau?
options: Removing all vegetation to plant more crops
Irrigating with overhead sprinklers at high pressure
Terracing to create level steps and reduce runoff speed
Heavy ploughing up and down the slope to loosen soil
questions.explanation: Terracing breaks slopes into level steps, slowing runoff and reducing erosion. Ploughing up and down increases erosion, removing vegetation exposes soil, and high-pressure overhead irrigation can wash away topsoil on slopes.

questions.q: On a map with scale 1:250,000, the straight-line distance between two towns measures 8 cm. What is the actual distance in kilometres?
options: 32 km
200 km
20 km
2 km
questions.explanation: Scale 1:250,000 means 1 cm = 2.5 km (because 250,000 cm = 2.5 km). So 8 cm = 8 × 2.5 = 20 km. 2 km, 32 km and 200 km are incorrect conversions.

questions.q: A contour interval on a topographic map is 20 m. If a hill summit is marked with a spot height of 360 m and the nearest closed contour below it is 340 m, what does this indicate?
options: The summit is 340 m because spot heights are approximate
The summit is 360 m high and lies between contours of 340 m and 360 m
The summit must be 380 m because contours only show even tens
The contour interval must be 10 m, so the map is inconsistent
questions.explanation: A spot height of 360 m gives the exact summit elevation; the nearest closed contour beneath is 340 m (next contour would be 360 m but the summit is marked within that area). 380 m is incorrect; spot heights are precise points, not approximate; the contour interval is stated as 20 m, so there is no inconsistency.

questions.q: Which of the following Nigerian cities is closest in climate to Lagos (tropical wet and dry with high humidity) rather than to Kano (semi-arid)?
options: Katsina
Sokoto
Port Harcourt
Maiduguri
questions.explanation: Port Harcourt in the Niger Delta has a humid tropical climate with high rainfall similar to Lagos, while Maiduguri, Katsina and Sokoto are in the northeastern and northwestern Sahel/semi-arid zones with much lower humidity and rainfall.

questions.q: The Niger Delta region contributes significantly to Nigeria's economy mainly because it:
options: contains large reserves of crude oil and associated gas
has the highest concentration of cotton mills
has the largest cocoa plantations in Nigeria
is the main source of iron ore for the country
questions.explanation: The Niger Delta's economic importance stems from its large petroleum reserves. Cocoa, iron ore and cotton-using industries are concentrated in other regions (southwest for cocoa, Itakpe area for iron ore, and northern textile areas for cotton).

questions.q: A community on the banks of the Niger River in Kogi State experiences seasonal flooding that deposits fertile silt but also destroys property. Which land-use practice would best reduce flood damage while preserving the floodplain fertility?
options: constructing permanent concrete levees around all settlements
filling and raising the entire floodplain to build houses
establishing setback zones where permanent buildings are prohibited and using floodplain for seasonal agriculture
draining the floodplain permanently to convert it to urban land
questions.explanation: Setback zones keep permanent structures away from flood-prone areas while allowing seasonal farming to benefit from silt. Raising or draining the floodplain destroys fertility and is costly; concrete levees can fail and remove natural floodplain functions.

questions.q: Which action would be most effective in reducing the frequency of wildfires in dry tropical woodland near Jos Plateau?
options: banning all use of fire for agriculture without alternatives
promoting controlled early-season burns and firebreaks managed by local communities
increasing grazing to remove all grasses immediately before the dry season
planting only fast-growing exotic trees throughout the woodland
questions.explanation: Controlled early burns and firebreaks reduce fuel loads and destructive late-season fires; outright bans without alternatives are impractical, exotic trees can increase fire risk or harm ecosystems, and overgrazing to remove grass is unsustainable and can cause erosion.

questions.q: If it is 09:00 GMT in London, what is the local time in Abuja (approximately 7°E) using standard time only?
questions.explanation: Abuja uses West Africa Time (UTC+1), one hour ahead of GMT, so 09:00 GMT = 10:00 local. 08:00 would be behind GMT, 11:00 is two hours ahead, and 09:30 incorrectly adds 30 minutes for longitude.

questions.q: Which mineral is most likely to scratch a steel knife (hardness ≈ 5.5) in a field test on a rock sample from Jos Plateau?
options: Quartz
Talc
Calcite
Gypsum
questions.explanation: Quartz has hardness 7 and will scratch steel; gypsum (2), calcite (3), and talc (1) are much softer and would not scratch a knife.

questions.q: A rock shows alternating bands of light and dark minerals and splits into thin sheets. This rock is most likely:
options: an igneous rock like basalt
a clastic sedimentary rock like sandstone
a metamorphic foliated rock such as schist
a chemical sedimentary rock like rock salt
questions.explanation: Foliation with alternating mineral bands and platy cleavage is characteristic of metamorphic rocks like schist. Basalt is fine-grained igneous without foliation, rock salt is chemical and non-foliated, and sandstone is clastic and lacks foliation.

questions.q: Which transport improvement would most increase the economic link between Kano and the port of Lagos?
options: constructing small riverside jetties on the Kano River
increasing the number of city bus routes within Kano
building more local airstrips near Kano for domestic flights
upgrading and maintaining the rail line linking Kano to southern ports
questions.explanation: A reliable rail connection reduces cost and time for bulk goods between Kano and Lagos. Local airstrips and city buses do not move large freight effectively, and Kano River jetties are impractical for ocean shipping.

questions.q: A community pays 5000 Naira per hectare per year to protect a nearby forest from illegal logging through community patrols. This payment is an example of:
options: an export tax on forest products
a payment for ecosystem services (PES) aimed at forest conservation
a government subsidy for timber extraction
a mandatory fine for community members
questions.explanation: Paying the community to conserve the forest is a PES scheme rewarding protection. It is not a subsidy for extraction, an export tax, or a fine imposed on residents.

questions.q: The town of Okigwe had a population of 120,000 in 2000 and 180,000 in 2010. What is the approximate annual population growth rate (compound)?
questions.explanation: Use (1 + r)^10 = 180000/120000 = 1.5, so 1 + r = 1.5^(0.1) ≈ 1.0414, r ≈ 0.0414 = 4.14%. The other choices are simple miscalculations: 3% or 5% would give totals different from 180,000 after 10 years.

questions.q: A Nigerian town has age groups: 0–14 years = 25,000; 15–64 years = 48,000; 65+ years = 7,000. What is the dependency ratio (dependents per 100 working-age people)?
questions.explanation: Dependency ratio = (25,000 + 7,000) / 48,000 × 100 = 32,000/48,000 × 100 = 66.666... ≈ 66.7. 52.1 and 33.3 are results of wrong numerator/denominator choices; 100 means dependents equal workers, which is not the case here.

questions.q: Large out-migration of young adults from a rural LGA in Kaduna State is most likely to cause which immediate demographic change in that rural area?
options: A rise in the proportion of young adults
An immediate increase in population density
A decline in the crude birth rate
A sudden rise in infant mortality
questions.explanation: Young adults are the main childbearing cohort; their out-migration reduces the number of births and so lowers the crude birth rate. It would not increase infant mortality directly, nor increase population density, and it reduces rather than raises the proportion of young adults.

questions.q: Which one of the following is the main disadvantage of strong urban primacy (one city far larger than others) in a country like Nigeria?
options: Greater rural development because people stay in villages
Lower international visibility of the largest city
Even distribution of industrial jobs across many small towns
Over-concentration of services and infrastructure leading to congestion and high living costs
questions.explanation: Urban primacy often causes a single city (e.g., Lagos) to attract most services and infrastructure, producing congestion and high costs. The other options are incorrect: primacy does not cause even job distribution, nor greater rural development, and it usually increases, not lowers, the city's international visibility.

questions.q: Which feature is most characteristic of a shanty town (informal settlement) on the outskirts of Kano?
options: Lack of formal land tenure and limited access to piped water and sanitation
High-rise planned apartment blocks with regulated services
Major industrial factories with formal employment contracts
Strictly enforced building codes and wide paved streets
questions.explanation: Shanty towns typically have informal or insecure land tenure and poor basic services like water and sanitation. The wrong options describe formal, planned urban areas or industrial zones, not informal settlements.

questions.q: A trader in Enugu wants to site a new weekly market to serve farmers from several villages. Which site factor is most important to maximise trade?
options: A site deep inside one village away from main routes
A steep hilltop with poor access but scenic views
A flat floodplain near the river that floods annually
Location at the junction of main roads connecting the villages (good situation)
questions.explanation: A market's situation—being at major road junctions—improves accessibility for sellers and buyers. A flood-prone site or one isolated from routes would deter traders; a steep inaccessible hilltop would reduce participation.

questions.topic: The earth and the solar system
questions.q: Which statement best explains why Nigeria experiences warm weather year-round but still has wet and dry seasons?
options: Because Nigeria is near the equator so it receives high solar radiation year-round, while seasonal shifts in wind systems (e.g., tropical maritime and continental air masses) cause wet and dry seasons
Because Nigeria's tilt is very different from the global tilt so it has no seasons
Because volcanic eruptions in Nigeria control rainfall patterns
Because the Earth's distance to the Sun changes greatly through the year affecting Nigeria's temperature
questions.explanation: Nigeria's equatorial latitude gives consistently high insolation, producing warm temperatures; seasonal movement of the ITCZ and alternating air masses bring wet and dry seasons. Earth's orbital distance change is too small to cause this, the axial tilt is the same globally, and volcanic eruptions are not the main seasonal driver.

questions.topic: The earth and the solar system
questions.q: A total lunar eclipse occurs when which of the following alignments happens?
options: Earth and Moon are at right angles relative to the Sun causing no shadow
Earth is between the Sun and the Moon and the Moon passes through Earth's shadow
Moon is between the Sun and the Earth casting a shadow on Earth
Sun is between the Earth and the Moon causing the Moon to be fully lit
questions.explanation: A lunar eclipse occurs when Earth blocks sunlight from reaching the Moon (Earth between Sun and Moon). The Moon between Sun and Earth would be a solar eclipse for observers on Earth; the other options describe configurations that do not produce a lunar eclipse.

questions.q: On a surface weather map, isobars are very close together over the Gulf of Guinea. What is the best interpretation?
options: Strong winds are present because a steep pressure gradient exists
Temperatures are much lower than surrounding areas
Air pressure is uniformly high across the region
Heavy convective rainfall is guaranteed at that location
questions.explanation: Close isobars indicate a strong pressure gradient force which produces strong winds. While strong winds can accompany storms, close isobars do not guarantee heavy convective rainfall; they imply variability in pressure, not uniform high pressure, and do not directly dictate temperature.

questions.q: Which climate description best fits the Koppen 'Aw' climate found in parts of northern Nigeria?
options: Hot desert climate with virtually no annual rainfall
Maritime equatorial climate with heavy rainfall all year
Cold temperate climate with year-round snow
Tropical savanna climate with distinct wet summer and dry winter (pronounced dry season)
questions.explanation: Koppen Aw denotes tropical savanna: warm year-round with a pronounced dry season in the low-sun months and a wet season in high-sun months. It is not cold temperate, not hyper-arid desert, nor constantly wet maritime equatorial climate.

questions.q: Which of the following processes is primarily responsible for the formation of river meanders in the lower course of the Niger River near Lokoja?
options: Lateral erosion and deposition on alternating banks causing sinuosity
Glacial plucking and abrasion
Tectonic uplift creating bends in the river
Vertical erosion deepening the channel uniformly
questions.explanation: Meanders form where lateral (sideways) erosion on outer banks and deposition on inner banks create sinuous bends, typical of a low-gradient lower course like near Lokoja. Vertical erosion would deepen rather than bend the channel; glacial processes do not apply in tropical Nigeria; tectonic uplift deforms landforms at larger scales, not the main cause of meanders.

questions.q: A steep-sided valley with a narrow floor and several waterfalls is most likely to have been formed by which set of processes?
options: Chemical weathering and soil creep
Wind abrasion in an arid environment
Marine erosion and longshore drift
Vertical river erosion and headward erosion in a youthful landscape
questions.explanation: Steep-sided valleys with waterfalls indicate active vertical erosion and retreat of river source (headward erosion) in a youthful stage. Wind abrasion and marine processes are irrelevant to an inland river valley; chemical weathering and soil creep produce gentler slopes, not steep-sided valleys with waterfalls.

questions.q: A block of coastal rock is undercut at its base by wave action and collapses, leaving a steep-backed, flat-topped platform. Which coastal feature has formed?
options: A tombolo
A spit
A wave-cut platform
A sand dune
questions.explanation: Undercutting and collapse of cliff faces by waves produces a wave-cut platform (flat area at base). A spit and tombolo are depositional features created by longshore drift; a sand dune is aeolian, not produced by wave undercutting.

questions.q: Which improvement would most increase the speed and reliability of moving perishable vegetables from Jos to Lagos?
options: Building an additional small rural market in Jos
Replacing road freight with bicycle couriers
Construction of a refrigerated (cold-chain) road freight corridor with improved pavements
Introducing higher road tolls to raise revenue
questions.explanation: Perishable vegetables need cold-chain and good road surfaces to reduce spoilage and travel time; improved pavements plus refrigerated trucks directly address speed and reliability. Adding a market in Jos doesn't improve transport to Lagos; higher tolls slow trade by raising costs; bicycle couriers cannot cover long distances between Jos and Lagos.

questions.q: A coastal port in Port Harcourt experiences repeated siltation reducing channel depth. Which action would best restore navigability for medium-sized cargo ships?
options: Periodic dredging of the navigation channel to maintain required depth
Raising import tariffs to reduce ship visits
Converting the port to handle only road transport
Planting mangroves along the outer beach
questions.explanation: Siltation reduces channel depth and dredging is the standard remedy to restore required draft for ships. Raising tariffs or changing cargo modality do not address silt deposits; planting mangroves may trap more sediment nearshore and won't remove silt in the channel.

questions.q: A trader in Kano wants to reduce transport costs when exporting groundnuts to Europe. Which strategy will most directly lower per-unit freight cost?
options: Packing each consignment in extra heavy boxes for protection
Selling at a lower price to buyers in Kano
Using only express air cargo for all shipments
Consolidating shipments to fill a container before export
questions.explanation: Consolidating goods increases shipment volume per container, lowering average freight cost per unit. Selling at a lower price reduces revenue but not freight cost per unit; heavier packing raises freight cost; air cargo is faster but much more expensive, increasing per-unit transport cost.

questions.q: Which characteristic makes the Jos Plateau attractive for tin mining?
options: Extensive coral limestone bedrock
Continuous volcanic activity exposing fresh magma
Abundant peat bogs and organic soils
Presence of shallow, concentrated cassiterite ore bodies in lateritic soils near the surface
questions.explanation: The Jos Plateau contains cassiterite concentrated in lateritic soils near surface, making tin mining economically feasible. Peat bogs, volcanic magma exposure, and coral limestone are not the geological conditions associated with tin deposits on the Plateau.

questions.q: A small-scale oil company extracts 2,400 barrels of crude oil per day and sells it at 1,200 Naira per barrel. If daily operating cost is 600,000 Naira, what is the daily profit?
questions.explanation: Revenue = 2,400 × 1,200 = 2,880,000 Naira. Profit = Revenue − Cost = 2,880,000 − 600,000 = 2,280,000 Naira. The other options either omit subtracting cost correctly or use incorrect multiplication.

questions.q: Which vegetation type and soil pairing best explains the dominance of oil palm cultivation in the Niger Delta?
options: Montane grassland with podzolic soils
Tropical rainforest vegetation with deep, fertile alluvial and deltaic soils
Mangrove vegetation with sandy desert soils
Sahel savanna with shallow calcareous soils
questions.explanation: The Niger Delta has rainforest/mangrove transition and deep alluvial/deltaic soils that support oil palm. Sahel savanna and montane grassland are wrong climates; mangroves exist but sandy desert soils do not occur there and are unsuitable for oil palm.

questions.q: A farmer in Anambra tests soil pH and finds pH = 5.0. Which amendment will most effectively raise the pH toward neutral for yam and cassava production?
options: Increasing irrigation with acidic rainwater
Adding elemental sulphur
Application of agricultural lime (calcium carbonate) at recommended rate
Applying ammonium sulphate fertilizer
questions.explanation: Acidic soil (pH 5.0) is best limed with calcium carbonate to raise pH. Elemental sulphur lowers pH further; acidic rainwater won't reliably raise pH; ammonium sulphate tends to acidify soils over time rather than neutralize acidity.

questions.q: A farmer in Oyo State intends to plant maize on a 4 ha field. Recommended planting density is 53,333 plants per hectare, and expected yield per plant is 0.25 kg. If he achieves the recommendation, what total yield (in tonnes) should he expect?
options: 53.333 tonnes
40 tonnes
13.333 tonnes
106.667 tonnes
questions.explanation: Total plants = 53,333 × 4 = 213,332. Yield = 213,332 × 0.25 kg = 53,333 kg = 53.333 tonnes. 13.333 t would be if yield per plant were 0.0625 kg; 106.667 t is double the correct value.

questions.q: Which soil management practice is most effective at reducing topsoil erosion on a steep cocoa farm on the Mambilla Plateau?
options: Burning undergrowth annually before planting
Contour planting with grass strips between rows
Deep ploughing up and down the slope
Planting pure stands of fast-growing eucalyptus
questions.explanation: Contour planting and grass strips slow runoff and trap sediment, reducing erosion. Deep ploughing down the slope and burning increase runoff and erosion. Pure eucalyptus tends to dry soil and reduce understorey, worsening erosion rather than preventing it.

questions.q: On a topographic map at scale 1:50,000, two towns A and B are 8.4 cm apart. What is the ground distance in kilometres between the towns?
options: 4.2 km
42 km
questions.explanation: Ground distance = 8.4 cm × 50,000 = 420,000 cm = 4,200 m = 4.2 km. 0.42 km would be if scale was 1:5,000; 42 km corresponds to 84 cm at 1:50,000; 16.8 km is double the correct value.

questions.q: A map shows a straight contour line labelled 200 m. Which conclusion about the land along that contour is correct?
options: Every point on that line is at an elevation of approximately 200 m above sea level
The land along that line has a slope of 200 m per kilometre
The highest point inside that contour is 200 m
The river crossing that contour is exactly 200 m deep
questions.explanation: A contour line joins points of equal elevation; thus points on it are at about 200 m. It does not indicate slope rate per unit distance. Highest point inside could be higher if enclosed by higher contours. Rivers being '200 m deep' is a misunderstanding of contour information.

questions.q: Using a map with grid north aligned with the top of the map, a student measures the bearing from town X to town Y as 135°. What is the compass direction from X to Y in conventional terms?
options: Southwest
Northeast
Southeast
Northwest
questions.explanation: A bearing of 135° is measured clockwise from north and points halfway between south and east, which is southeast. Northeast is 45°, southwest is 225°, northwest is 315°.

questions.q: Which Nigerian city is best described as a major oil refining and river port in the Niger Delta region?
options: Port Harcourt
Maiduguri
Kano
Jos
questions.explanation: Port Harcourt is a major oil refining centre and river port in the Niger Delta. Jos is a plateau mining centre, Kano is a northern trade and manufacturing city, Maiduguri is in the northeast near Lake Chad.

questions.q: Which factor most explains why Lagos developed into Nigeria's largest city earlier than other Nigerian cities?
options: Its sheltered natural harbour and position as a coastal port for Atlantic trade
Its location on a high plateau ideal for cereals
Its isolation from major trade routes
Its proximity to the Jos tin fields
questions.explanation: Lagos grew early because of its excellent harbour and coastal location facilitating Atlantic trade. It is not near the Jos tin fields, not on a high plateau, and certainly not isolated from trade routes.

questions.q: A community along the Ogun River experiences annual flooding in the rainy season. Which long-term measure would best reduce flood damage while allowing river function?
options: Restoring wetlands and floodplains upstream to store peak flows
Building higher concrete walls along the entire riverbank
Dredging the river channel to its maximum depth every year
Clearing all vegetation from riverbanks to allow faster flow
questions.explanation: Restoring wetlands/floodplains increases storage of peak flows and reduces downstream flooding while preserving river ecology. Continuous high walls are expensive and can worsen upstream flooding; excessive dredging may destabilize banks and increase sediment downstream; clearing vegetation increases erosion and peak flows.

questions.q: In a forest reserve near Jos, miners have exposed soil and left tailings that leach heavy metals into nearby streams. Which immediate remediation step will most rapidly reduce metal runoff into the streams?
options: Installing shallow wells to lower the water table across the catchment
Building gravel footpaths for miners to reduce trampling
Introducing fish species that consume metals
Covering exposed tailings with impermeable liners and re-vegetating the area
questions.explanation: Covering tailings with liners and re-vegetation prevents rainwater infiltration and surface erosion, reducing metal runoff. Lowering the water table is not effective for surface leaching; footpaths do not stop runoff; fish cannot remove dissolved heavy metals and introducing species can cause ecological harm.

questions.q: A farmer near Ijebu-Ode measures a rectangular cocoa plot on a 1:50,000 topographic map as 6.2 cm by 3.4 cm. What is the actual area of the plot in hectares?
options: 527 ha
questions.explanation: At 1:50,000 scale 1 cm = 500 m. So 6.2 cm = 6.2 × 500 m = 3,100 m and 3.4 cm = 3.4 × 500 m = 1,700 m. Area = 3,100 m × 1,700 m = 5,270,000 m². Convert to hectares: 5,270,000 ÷ 10,000 = 527 ha. The other options come from decimal-place errors (dividing or multiplying by 10 or 1,000 incorrectly).

questions.q: On a topographic map at scale 1:50,000, the straight-line distance between two towns is 7.2 cm. What is the actual ground distance between the towns in kilometres?
options: 3.6 km
72 km
36 km
questions.explanation: Scale 1:50,000 means 1 cm on the map = 50,000 cm on the ground = 500 m. So 7.2 cm × 500 m/cm = 3600 m = 3.6 km. 72 km would result from misreading the scale as 1:1,000,000; 36 km comes from treating 1 cm as 5 km (i.e. 1:500,000); 0.72 km is off by a factor of 5 (treating 1 cm = 100 m).
